body.statement: For every fixed \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{hist}}(b,L)\), under iid sampling and the all-data Beta histogram posterior with \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\), a sufficiently large deterministic constant in \(H_n\) gives \(\Pi_n(H_n\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n)\to1\) in \(P\)-probability. Moreover, \[\sup_{\eta\in H_n}|\mathbb G_n(m_\eta-m_P)|\to0\] in outer \(P\)-probability. The proof must retain posterior cap crossings, use the minimum expected arm count of order \(n/J_n^2\), and localize changing branches to at most \(2J_n\rho_n+4\) bins. In particular, \(\sqrt n\{\rho_n\varepsilon_n+\rho_n^2\}\to0\).
body.justification: This is the load-bearing new probability theorem that turns an abstract one-step posterior transfer into an explicit cap-crossing Bayesian procedure.
body.gap: Castillo controls a single density histogram; Yiu et al. and Schmidt--Wikle require rather than derive this joint unequal-arm contraction and posterior-indexed threshold equicontinuity.
body.consumer: Users of conjugate Bayesian nuisance models obtain a fully specified, all-data calibration theorem without sample splitting or a no-crossing restriction.
